name: Cubbon Park
description: A 300-acre Victorian-era lung of the city, with tree tunnels, statues, and a calm walking grid between government buildings.
foodTip: Grab a filter coffee after your walk at nearby Indian Coffee House or a kiosk near the park gates.
cultureNote: Laid out in 1870 and still the city's favourite shade. Early mornings fill with walkers, yoga groups, and newspaper readers.

name: Vidhana Soudha
description: Karnataka's granite neo-Dravidian legislature, floodlit at night and imposing by day. Best admired from the lawns opposite.
foodTip: No food inside the complex — plan a snack on Infantry Road afterwards.
cultureNote: The Kannada inscription on the entablature reads 'Government Work is God's Work'.

name: Attara Kacheri (High Court)
description: A red-brick Greco-Roman courthouse facing Vidhana Soudha — two architectural eras in one glance.
foodTip: Walk a few minutes to Koshy's for bun-butter-jam and coffee after photos.
cultureNote: Built in 1868 as the public offices, it is one of Bengaluru's most photographed colonial facades.

name: Visvesvaraya Industrial Museum
description: Hands-on science museum named after engineer-statesman M. Visvesvaraya. Fun even if you only wander the aircraft and engine halls.
foodTip: Airlines Hotel on Madras Bank Road is a short walk for thali and kesari bath.
cultureNote: A favourite school-trip landmark that still surprises adults with the outdoor engine park.

name: St. Mark's Cathedral
description: A pale, domed Anglican cathedral from 1812, tucked just off the MG Road rush. Quiet interiors and a leafy compound.
foodTip: Church Street bakeries and coffee shops are two minutes away.
cultureNote: One of the oldest churches in the city; the dome is a useful landmark when you are walking the cantonment grid.

name: Rangoli Metro Art Center
description: An open-air gallery along the MG Road metro walkway — murals, pop-up crafts, and city photography under the elevated tracks.
foodTip: Exit toward Church Street for pizza, filter coffee, or chaat within a block.
cultureNote: Built as a public art spine so commuters actually linger on the walking deck.

name: Blossom Book House
description: A beloved multi-floor used-and-new bookstore. Easy to lose 25 minutes in the poetry and travel shelves.
foodTip: The only rule: do not skip a coffee on Church Street before or after.
cultureNote: A rite of passage for Bengaluru readers; bargain tables change daily.

name: Church Street food stretch
description: Bengaluru's most walkable cafe-and-night-out lane: bookstores, bars, dosa counters, and live music spill onto the pavement.
foodTip: Try a local craft beer, a wood-fired pizza, or late-night kati rolls depending on the hour.
cultureNote: The street is pedestrian-friendly in the evenings and a snapshot of the city's social life.

name: Brigade Road
description: Neon, sneakers, streetwear, and people-watching. A classic tourist stroll connecting MG Road to Richmond Town.
foodTip: Look for shawarma, juice, and old-school ice cream parlours on the side lanes.
cultureNote: Once the fashionable spine of the cantonment; still the easiest place to feel the city's weekend energy.

name: Commercial Street
description: A dense bazaar for clothes, jewellery, and bargaining. Come with patience and a light backpack.
foodTip: Duck into a side lane for kebabs, haleem (in season), or a quick chaat.
cultureNote: The street mixes Tamil, Urdu, and Kannada shopfronts — a living map of the old cantonment trade.

name: Russell Market
description: A 1920s red-brick market for flowers, meat, and produce. Atmospheric, busy, and very local.
foodTip: Breakfast nearby: bun muska, sulaimani chai, or a hearty Muslim-style biryani later in the day.
cultureNote: Built for the cantonment and still the wholesale heart of Shivajinagar.

name: St. Mary's Basilica
description: Bengaluru's only basilica — Gothic towers, stained glass, and a famous September feast.
foodTip: Combine with Russell Market; tea stalls sit right outside the compound.
cultureNote: A pilgrimage church for the city's Catholic community and a striking skyline marker.

name: Ulsoor Lake
description: A wide lake with a walking path, islands, and evening breeze. Gentler than Cubbon, more neighbourhood than monument.
foodTip: Halasuru has excellent darshini breakfasts if you time a morning loop.
cultureNote: One of the city's oldest tanks, still used by walkers, boat clubs, and festival processions.

name: Halasuru Someshwara Temple
description: A Chola-era temple with later Vijayanagara work — dravida vimana, stone pillars, and a surprisingly quiet courtyard.
foodTip: Temple-area darshinis serve crisp vada and coffee from dawn.
cultureNote: Proof that Bengaluru's sacred geography is older than the garden-city myth.

name: Bangalore Palace
description: A Tudor-style palace with stained glass, stuffed trophies, and sprawling grounds. Ticketed interiors are worth it if you have 45 minutes.
foodTip: Palace Grounds food trucks appear on event days; otherwise head toward Malleswaram for tiffin.
cultureNote: Inspired by Windsor and still owned by the Wadiyar family.

name: Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath
description: Art college, galleries, and a famous folk-bronze collection. A calm indoor pause on a hot walk.
foodTip: Walk toward Malleswaram 8th Cross for Veena Stores or CTR-style tiffin nearby.
cultureNote: A hub for Karnataka's contemporary and traditional visual arts.

name: Sankey Tank
description: A landscaped tank with a popular jogging path, sunset light, and ice-cream carts on weekends.
foodTip: Malleswaram bakeries and chaat are a short detour south.
cultureNote: Built in the 1880s as a reservoir; now a neighbourhood ritual more than a tourist stop.

name: Veena Stores
description: Tiny, legendary idli-vada counter. Eat standing, eat fast, and do not expect a menu speech.
foodTip: Thatte idli, vada, and chutney. Come before 10:30 if you hate queues.
cultureNote: Malleswaram breakfast is a Bengaluru personality test — this is the classic score.

name: 8th Cross Malleswaram
description: A village-like shopping street: flowers, silk, banana stems, and old bakeries under rain trees.
foodTip: Filter coffee + khara bun is the correct order of operations.
cultureNote: Old Bengaluru in one stretch — Kannada signboards, temple bells, and vegetable bargaining.

name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
description: Hyder Ali's garden, a Glass House, a 3-billion-year-old rock, and flower shows that take over the city calendar.
foodTip: MTR on Lalbagh Road is the pilgrimage pairing: rava idli, masala dosa, and filter coffee.
cultureNote: A botanical archive of colonial plant hunting and a daily park for South Bengaluru.

name: MTR (Lalbagh Road)
description: The original Mavalli Tiffin Room. Formal-ish, fast, and serious about rava idli.
foodTip: Rava idli, khara bath, and coffee. Lunch thalis are excellent if you arrive hungry.
cultureNote: A 1924 institution that exported Bengaluru tiffin to the world without softening it.

name: Dodda Basavana Gudi (Bull Temple)
description: A giant monolith Nandi on Bugle Rock. Short visit, big payoff, granite under your feet.
foodTip: Vidyarthi Bhavan and Gandhi Bazaar snacks are the natural next stop.
cultureNote: Kempe Gowda-era Bengaluru — the bull is said to watch over the old pete.

name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
description: The dosa that launched a thousand arguments. Crisp, buttery, and served with theatre.
foodTip: Masala dosa only. Share if you must; do not skip the butter.
cultureNote: A 1943 student canteen that became a city shrine. Queues are part of the ritual.

name: Gandhi Bazaar
description: Flower stalls, banana stems, and the smell of jasmine. Best in the morning when the market is loudest.
foodTip: Chaat, mangoes in season, and a stop at a darshini for khara.
cultureNote: The social square of old South Bengaluru, especially around festivals.

name: Bugle Rock Park
description: Ancient granite outcrop with a small park, sunset views, and fruit bats in the trees at dusk.
foodTip: Combine with Bull Temple and a Gandhi Bazaar snack.
cultureNote: Kempe Gowda's watchmen once sounded bugles from this rock.

name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
description: A teak palace with floral pillars and a small museum. Compact, shaded, and rich with 18th-century politics.
foodTip: KR Market fruit and sugarcane juice are around the corner.
cultureNote: Built as a summer retreat while the stone fort still defined Bengaluru pete.

name: Bengaluru Fort
description: Remaining stone walls of the old fort beside the city market. A short, grounding stop before the chaos of KR Market.
foodTip: Market grapes, mosambi juice, and flower garlands immediately outside.
cultureNote: Kempe Gowda's mud fort, later rebuilt in stone by Hyder and Tipu.

name: KR Market (City Market)
description: The city's wholesale flower-and-produce theatre. Go early, keep pockets zipped, and look up at the heritage market building.
foodTip: Fresh fruit, tender coconut, and legendary flower streets. Eat cooked food at a trusted stall, not from the gutter edge.
cultureNote: Named after Krishnarajendra Wadiyar. At dawn it is one of the most cinematic places in India.

name: Sultan Jamia Masjid
description: A grand mosque by the old fort — white facades, busy lanes, and the sound of the pete.
foodTip: Pete biryani and wood-fired roti shops sit in the surrounding streets.
cultureNote: Spiritual centre of the old market quarter.

name: UB City
description: A high-rise mixed-use complex with public art, shops, and a skyline view of a newer Bengaluru.
foodTip: Upscale dining inside; Cubbon Park street fruit is two minutes away if you want contrast.
cultureNote: A symbol of 2000s Bengaluru money, useful as a landmark between Cubbon and Lavelle Road.

name: Lavelle Road
description: Cafes, galleries, and trees. The slowest fashionable walk in central Bengaluru.
foodTip: Brunch culture, kombucha, and also old clubs just off the road. Pick your century.
cultureNote: Named after a 19th-century Irish soldier; now the city's boutique-cafe spine.

name: Koshy's
description: A 1940s restaurant-bar where journalists, theatre people, and tourists share the same slow fans.
foodTip: Bun-butter-jam, roast pork, or a simple omelette. Stay for the room, not just the plate.
cultureNote: If Bengaluru has a living room, this is a strong candidate.

name: Airlines Hotel
description: An old garden restaurant with thalis, dosas, and a slightly time-warped courtyard.
foodTip: Breakfast in the open air: dosa, coffee, and newspaper energy.
cultureNote: A surviving clubby eatery from when this was still a quiet cantonment pocket.

name: Freedom Park
description: A former central jail turned public park and protest ground, with preserved prison blocks.
foodTip: Gandhinagar and Majestic have cheap meals; walk toward Cubbon for shade.
cultureNote: A rare civic space that keeps the city's political memory in the open.

name: Indiranagar cafe stretch
description: 100 Feet Road and its cross streets: specialty coffee, bakeries, and a younger nightlife than Church Street.
foodTip: Filter coffee 2.0, sourdough, and also excellent South Indian in the inner roads.
cultureNote: The neighbourhood that taught Bengaluru how to brunch.

name: Defence Colony park pocket
description: Tree-lined inner roads and a small park grid — the residential calm behind 100 Feet Road.
foodTip: Breakfast at a neighbourhood bakery, then coffee on the main road.
cultureNote: Shows the garden-city layout that still hides behind Bengaluru's busiest retail streets.

name: M. Chinnaswamy Stadium
description: Home of RCB and a cricket cathedral. Even without a match, the gates and crowd energy are part of the city.
foodTip: Match days mean street food; other days walk to MG Road for a proper meal.
cultureNote: On big IPL nights this corner of Cubbon becomes a festival.

name: Venkatappa Art Gallery
description: A compact state gallery next to the museum complex. Good for a 20-minute art pause.
foodTip: Cubbon Park south gate snacks, or walk to UB City.
cultureNote: Named after the artist K. Venkatappa, a key figure in the Mysore school.

name: Cubbon Park bandstand
description: An open octagonal bandstand used for weekend music and idle sitting under rain trees.
foodTip: Carry water; the nearest good coffee is toward MG Road or Indian Coffee House.
cultureNote: A leftover of colonial park entertainment that locals still use as a meeting pin.

name: Richmond Park / field edge
description: A green pause between Brigade Road and the older bungalow streets of Richmond Town.
foodTip: Richmond Town bakeries and Armenian Street cafes sit nearby.
cultureNote: Part of the cantonment's original open-space pattern.

name: St. Patrick's Church
description: A tall Gothic church off Brigade Road, cooler inside than the shopping street it hides from.
foodTip: Brigade Road snacks immediately after.
cultureNote: A reminder that the cantonment was built as much around churches as clubs.
